name: showreel-20-hover

voice.text: Why does your button stay lit after tapping? Phones fake a hover when you tap. And it sticks, until you tap somewhere else. The fix: wrap your hover rule in at media, hover, hover. Now only a mouse gets the hover. On a phone, a tap is just a tap.

caption:
Why does your button stay lit after tapping? 👆

On a phone there's no mouse, so a tap counts as a hover. In some mobile browsers the :hover style then sticks after your finger lifts, until you tap somewhere else. Wrap your hover styles in @media (hover: hover) and only devices that can really hover (a mouse, a trackpad) get them; on a phone, a tap is just a tap. One media query, in every major browser. (A few Android phones report hover wrongly; add and (pointer: fine) to be safe. Keep an :active style for tap feedback.)
Save it for your next button, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

sources.note: MDN :hover: on touchscreens it may never match, match only for a moment, or keep matching after the touch ends until the user touches another element
MDN hover media feature: hover = the primary input can conveniently hover; none = many mobile devices only emulate hovering
@media (hover): Chrome 38, Chrome Android 50, Firefox 64, Safari 9; some Samsung Android devices may wrongly match (hover: hover) (crbug 41445959)

tip.title: Why does your button stay lit after tapping?
tip.why: On a touchscreen there is no pointer resting on the page, so mobile browsers emulate hover on tap, and depending on the browser the :hover style can stay on after the finger lifts, until the user touches something else (MDN). Put hover styles inside @media (hover: hover): only devices whose main input can really hover (a mouse, a trackpad) get them, and on a phone a tap is just a tap. A few Android devices report hover wrongly, so add and (pointer: fine) if you need to be sure, and keep an :active style for tap feedback.
